Alex: quick heads-up — ran into a nasty case where slab boundaries + sparse KV yields bad attention kernel assumptions :grimacing:
Alex: summary: when a request triggers eviction that splits a token range across two slabs, some kernels that assume contiguous KV slices blow up or do extra memcpy
Maria: can you paste the minimal repro stack/logs?
Alex: yep, attaching snippet — reproduced with short seq lengths + aggressive slab size 16k:
```
// evict: slabA[0..1023], slabB[1024..2047]
KVLookup: returns two fragments
AttentionKernel: expects single contiguous KV buf, panics on non-contig
```

Dinesh: hmm, we've always leaned on contiguous KV for performance. Two options: 1) add kernel-side frag handling (merge/iterate), 2) keep kernels lean and add a small merge buffer when fragmentation detected
Olivia: option 2 seems simpler to maintain, but copying undermines batching perf. Need numbers: cost per token copy vs complexity cost of kernel changes
Sam: +1 on measuring. Also we should consider pinning: avoid evicting slabs that hold the tail of an active KV chain during generation
Zara: is refcounting per-slice feasible? i.e., increment refcount when KV used by an inflight request, GC only when refcount==0. That prevents mid-gen splits
Alex: refcounts would reduce races but increases metadata and lock complexity. Also doesn't avoid fragmentation from prior evictions — you'd still have multiple fragments for a single logical range
Maria: what about a hybrid: quick merge buffer for small fragment counts (<=2), kernel negotiation flag for models that can handle fragmented KV natively
Alex: prototype flag idea: on model init, kernel exposes capability: `supports_fragmented_kv: true|false`. Serving runtime queries that and either passes fragments or coalesces
Dinesh: love that. Keeps kernel complexity optional. For kernels that support fragments, we should expose an iterator API rather than changing memory layout: something like `kv_iter(ctx, callback(fragment_base, len, stride))`
Olivia: iterator API sounds elegant but could limit vectorized kernels. Could be a perf cliff for SIMD codepaths
Sam: right — kernels with SIMD prefer contiguous arrays. So for those we fallback to copy into an aligned scratch buffer. Need to size buffer heuristically (merge at most N tokens)
Alex: proposed config snippet for runtime tunables:
```
kv_compat:
  require_contiguous_for_simd: true
  max_fragments_to_merge: 2
  merge_scratch_pool_size: 8MB
```

Zara: we should also add an async background defragmenter: when load low, coalesce fragmented ranges to reduce future copies
Maria: perf plan: Dinesh + Olivia measure copy cost for 1..8 fragments vs implementing small iterator loop in kernel. Alex prototype coalescing buffer. Zara sketch defrag design. I'll update the RFC with a negotiation field and tunables
Dinesh: question — what about memory lifetime? If we hand fragment pointers to kernels, we must guarantee they remain valid for kernel duration. So either pin slabs or copy. Need clear ownership model in the API
Alex: agreed. Kernel contract: pointers are valid only during single request callback; no async retention. We'll document that and enforce via refcount/pin for inflight requests
ci-bot: note — created issue #2371: "kv-fragment-support-handshake" from thread by Alex
Sam: action items: Olivia prototype merge buffer + measurement (ETA 2d); Dinesh experiment kernel iterator benchmark (ETA 1w); Zara design async defrag PR (ETA 2w); Maria update RFC (ETA 3d) :+1:
Alex: thanks all. keeping this thread as the design anchor. ping me if you need test harness for reproducer :rocket:
